title: Your First Engineering Experiment
summary: Great engineers don't just guess what happens—they use the Scientific Engineering Method:

steps.title: Your First Engineering Experiment
steps.markdownContent: Engineers test ideas. First predict what will happen. Then run one test, watch closely, and compare the result with your prediction.

quickCheck.question: What should an engineer do BEFORE running a test or experiment?
options: Predict what they expect will happen
Close their eyes and hope for the best
Toss the board across the room
quickCheck.explanation: Making a thoughtful prediction helps you see if your experiment worked the way you expected!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: Predicting means thinking ahead about what should happen before you run a test.

quickCheck.question: Where is the built-in test LED located on your Arduino Uno board?
options: Connected to Pin 13, labeled with the letter 'L'
quickCheck.explanation: The built-in LED is right on the board next to Pin 13 and labeled 'L'!
quickCheck.warmupExplanation: The Arduino has a tiny light on the board labeled 'L' so you can test code without extra wires.

steps.title: The Scientific Engineering Method
steps.markdownContent: A fair test changes one thing at a time. Write or say: “I thought ___. I tried ___. I noticed ___.”

steps.title: Formulate Your Prediction & Test
steps.markdownContent: Predict what the L light will do, run the virtual test, and compare what happened with your prediction.

steps.title: Engineering Method Checkpoint
steps.markdownContent: Verify your understanding of experimental engineering methods!

interactiveConfig.question: Why is forming a prediction before running a test essential for engineers?
options: It forces you to understand the logic and lets you verify if hardware behaves as expected
It makes the computer run ten times faster
It prevents the USB cable from being plugged in
interactiveConfig.explanation: Predicting outcome requires analyzing how code and circuit interface together, enabling meaningful verification.
